name: Uveal Melanoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Uveal Melanoma

criteria.description: Presence of a pigmented or non-pigmented intraocular mass in the uveal tract detected by ophthalmoscopy or ultrasonography
High internal reflectivity and acoustic hollowness on ocular ultrasonography consistent with melanoma
Histopathological confirmation of malignant melanocytic tumor cells in the uveal tract
Characteristic vascular patterns on fluorescein angiography supporting diagnosis
Detection of monosomy 3 or mutations in GNAQ/GNA11 genes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of an intraocular uveal mass with characteristic imaging features; histopathological confirmation if biopsy or enucleation performed
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; biopsy is not always performed due to risk of tumor dissemination.

laboratory: Liver function tests may be elevated in metastatic disease
Serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) may be increased with metastasis
imaging: Ocular ultrasonography showing dome-shaped choroidal mass with low to medium internal reflectivity
Fundus photography demonstrating pigmented or amelanotic lesion
Fluorescein angiography revealing intrinsic tumor vasculature
MRI of orbit showing intraocular mass with characteristic signal intensities
CT or MRI of liver for metastatic screening
other: Histopathology showing malignant melanocytic cells with spindle or epithelioid morphology
Fine needle aspiration biopsy may be used for cytological diagnosis

distinguishingFeatures: Smaller size and stable appearance over time
Lack of subretinal fluid or orange pigment
No documented growth on serial imaging

redFlags: Rapid increase in size of intraocular mass
New onset of visual field defects or vision loss
Evidence of metastatic disease (e.g., hepatomegaly, respiratory symptoms)
references: Shields CL, Shields JA. Uveal melanoma: clinical features and diagnosis. In: Shields Textbook of Ophthalmology. 7th ed. 2020.
Carvajal RD, Schwartz GK, Tezel T, et al. Metastatic disease from uveal melanoma: treatment options and future prospects. Br J Ophthalmol. 2017;101(1):38-44.
